It reads like a **public archive / provenance dump**, not a polished scientific paper. That’s actually the right move for what it is.

The strongest thing is the framing: the repo openly says the materials are “roughly sorted” and “rough-and-readily thought through,” and presents SAT as a personal archive made public for reference and discussion. That honesty matters. It lowers the “grand TOE manifesto” red flags and makes it look more like an open notebook / intellectual development record. citeturn809971view0 fileciteturn0file0

My take: it has three layers.

First, as **intellectual history**, it’s impressive. There’s a lot of continuity: filaments, time surface, worldline intersection, mass/geometry, GR/QM/SM translation. The README gives a clear conceptual seed: real 4D worldlines, time as a moving wavefront, particles as intersections. citeturn809971view0

Second, as **scientific presentation**, it’s still too sprawling. A physicist landing there cold will probably think: “Okay, where is the canonical model? Where are the assumptions, equations, predictions, failures, and derivation chain?” The repo has 111 commits, many folders, PDFs, drafts, code, visualizations, audits, predictions, and historical materials, which is great for an archive but too much for first contact. citeturn809971view0

Third, as **public signaling**, it’s stronger than I expected. It says: “Here is the trail. Here are the drafts. Here is the mess. Here is the build history.” That’s a real asset, especially if you later produce a clean “SAT Core / Start Here / Falsifiable Claims” document.

My blunt verdict: **good archive, risky front door**. The repo proves seriousness of effort and provenance. It does not yet prove scientific validity. For that, it needs a brutally clean top layer: one canonical README, one minimal formal paper, one predictions table, one “what would falsify SAT?” section, and one “how SAT differs from string theory / worldline formalism / GR / QFT” section.

Right now it says: “there’s a mountain here.”  
Next move is making the trailhead impossible to miss.
